title: Gold Surges to Two-Week High Above $4,100 as Iran Strikes Revive Safe-Haven Bid
excerpt: Comex gold settled up 1.86% at $4,146.90 as the US-Iran conflict escalated into its 11th night of airstrikes, with analysts eyeing $4,375 as the near-term target.
body:
• Gold prices surged to a two-week high of $4,146.90 amid escalating tensions between the US and Iran.
  • Brent crude oil prices rose above $95, enhancing gold's attractiveness as an inflation hedge.
  • Despite geopolitical tensions, the Federal Reserve's hawkish stance limits gold's potential for further gains.
  • Central bank purchases, particularly from China, provide ongoing structural support for gold prices.
Key Takeaways
  • Gold reached a two-week high of $4,146.90 amid escalating US-Iran conflict.
  • Brent crude oil prices surged above $95, boosting gold's appeal as an inflation hedge.
  • The Federal Reserve's hawkish stance limits gold's upside potential despite geopolitical tensions.
  • Central bank purchases, including China's, provide a structural support for gold prices.

Gold surged to its highest level in two weeks on Wednesday, reclaiming the $4,100 mark as renewed hostilities between the United States and Iran drove investors back into the metal. Spot XAU/USD traded near $4,112.70, while August Comex futures settled up $75.80 — or 1.86% — at $4,146.90 per troy ounce, according to Dow Jones Market Data.

The rally marks gold's largest single-day dollar gain since June 15 and pushes it to its highest settlement since July 6. It extends a pattern seen repeatedly this year: geopolitical shocks overriding the bearish pull of elevated Treasury yields and a firm US dollar.

War Premium Returns After Ceasefire Collapses

The catalyst is straightforward. A 60-day ceasefire between Washington and Tehran, signed last month, collapsed in early July. The US military has now carried out 11 consecutive nights of airstrikes against Iranian targets, a campaign that defense officials told Congress has cost $37.5 billion to date. Iran's Revolutionary Guards warned on X that the Strait of Hormuz's southern route is mined, and Houthi militants in Yemen announced a naval blockade of Saudi Arabia.

Earlier this month, fading tensions had drained gold's war premium, pulling the metal back toward the $4,000–$4,050 zone. That calm proved short-lived. As the conflict re-escalated, capital rotated sharply back into gold and other traditional havens.

"Prices are in an upswing that could continue until the end of the year. Central bank buying is starting to return after taking a pause."

— Peter Cardillo, Spartan Capital Securities

Cardillo set his near-term gold price target at $4,375 a troy ounce, noting that next week's Federal Reserve meeting on July 29 may provide more clarity on the interest rate trajectory.

Oil Surge Cuts Both Ways for the Metal

Brent crude surging above $95 a barrel — its highest since early June — has amplified gold's rally through a dual channel. Rising energy prices bolster the metal's appeal as an inflation hedge, while the supply disruption fears that drove oil higher simultaneously feed safe-haven demand.

But the relationship is not straightforward. Higher oil also stokes inflation expectations, which in turn raise the probability of further Fed tightening. The federal funds rate sits at 3.50%–3.75%, with roughly 85.6% odds of a hold at the July 29 meeting but approximately two-thirds probability of at least a quarter-point hike by September. Rising real yields increase the opportunity cost of holding gold, which pays no income.

Silver followed gold higher, with front-month Comex silver climbing 2.01% to $60.019 per troy ounce — its fourth consecutive session of gains and a cumulative 7.37% rise over that stretch.

For NRI Investors, Multiple Channels in Play

Indian investors tracking gold face a more complex picture than the dollar price alone suggests. Gold's rupee-denominated return depends on both the dollar price and the USD/INR exchange rate, which has seen the rupee weaken as oil-driven current account pressures mount.

India remains the world's second-largest gold consumer, and any sustained rally feeds directly into domestic jewelry and investment demand. The Reserve Bank of India has been among the central banks accumulating reserves — a structural bid that reinforces gold's floor from the supply side.

What to Watch Next

Central Bank Influence on Gold
›China added 14.93 tonnes of gold in June.
›Central bank buying supports gold price stability.
›India remains the second-largest gold consumer.

The July 29 Fed meeting is the next major catalyst. Hawkish guidance could cap gold below the $4,150–$4,200 resistance zone, while a dovish tilt would clear the path toward $4,375 and beyond. Equally critical is the trajectory of the Middle East conflict: a diplomatic breakthrough could drain the war premium as quickly as it returned, while further escalation — particularly any disruption to Strait of Hormuz shipping — could push gold toward its January record above $5,300.

Gold settled the day up 3.41% over two sessions, off 22.03% from its 2026 high of $5,318.40 set in January, but up 25.92% from its 52-week low. Year-to-date, the metal remains down 4.13%, underscoring that despite the haven bid, gold has yet to recapture the ground lost to the rate cycle.
